messages.author: 6a3b777d6a18967b
messages.subject: Problems after "Clean and Rebuild"
parts:
I just started my first package on github and some (not all) users are reporting that they cannot run the package after installing it.  I believe that I can reproduce the problem when I click "Clean and Rebuild" and try to run a trivial example:

df = data.frame(region=state.abb, value=sample(100, 50))
choroplethr(df, lod="state")

 Error in generate_values(choropleth$value, num_buckets) : 
  could not find function "cut2" 

cut2 is in Hmisc is listed as an Import in my DESCRIPTION file, so I'm not sure why it can't be found.  It can be found if I replace "cut2" with "Hmisc::cut2".  I guess the obvious question to ask is this: when writing a package, do all calls to functions from other packages need to include the package name?  

After fixing that error I then get another:

    choropleth = ggplot(choropleth, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group)) + 
                    geom_polygon(aes(fill = value), color = "black") +
                    scale_fill_brewer(scaleName, labels=comma) + # use brewer discrete scale
                    ggtitle(title) +
                    theme_clean();

Error in structure(list(call = match.call(), aesthetics = aesthetics,  : 
  object 'comma' not found

I am actually not sure where comma is defined, or why the line above this, which uses plyr, does not cause an error. 

Thanks.

Ari

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Problems after "Clean and Rebuild"
parts:
Hi Ari,

Welcome to the wonderful world of namespace debugging. The first tool
to help you is load_all(export_all = FALSE) - this makes load_all()
work more like library(), hiding the functions that are not explicitly
documented. export_all = FALSE makes it easier to iterate as you
figure out which functions need to be imported from other packages.

From the current messages it sounds like you need something like:

#' @importFrom Hmisc cut2
#' @importFrom scales comma

You'll need to do that for every function you use from another
package. Alternatively, as you discovered you can also skip importing
the function into your namespace and refer to it directly with ::.

Hadley
